query: [PHOTO] A handwritten enquiry list photographed on a phone. One product word is written ambiguously enough that it cannot be read with confidence; the other lines are legible with their quantities.
ground_truth: Intake must read the legible lines and their quantities correctly from the image. For the word it cannot read with confidence it must call verify_catalogue_term to check the reading against the catalogue rather than committing to a guess - and if the term is still not a real catalogue term, the line must be left for a human rather than silently corrected to the nearest plausible product. A quantity that cannot be read must be recorded as unreadable and must never be priced. The photo itself must be shown on the approval card so a human can compare it against the extracted lines, because a confident misreading of handwriting passes every code check.
why: The only case whose failure mode is a CONFIDENT wrong answer rather than an uncertain one, which is why the human comparison against the photo is part of the expected outcome rather than an optional extra.
